codex:
Verdict: RETRY once on the same angle. The reviewer’s numerical premise is false under the proposal’s own definition of V*: at p=1/2 and u>=3ell, p*=3/4 for (sigma1,sigma0)=(u,ell), so V*=4u^2/3+4ell^2 and the regret is 2u^2/3-2ell^2, not 0. The real defect is that the theorem does not explicitly take/prove the supremum over the full variance box and its tuple-order notation is ambiguous. For p_n=floor(n/2)/n<=1/2, the worst orientation is sigma1=u,sigma0=ell (i.e. tuple (ell,u) if vectors are ordered (sigma0,sigma1)); at even n the swapped orientation ties.

Verbatim angle directive:
"Repair only the one-batch anchor, without changing the topic, assumptions, exact-B frontier, two-batch claim, or any constants. Start from the definitions and state the finite-n identity as
Psi^=_{n,1}=min_{q in {ceil(n/4),...,floor(3n/4)}} sup_{sigma0,sigma1 in [ell,u]} {sigma1^2/(q/n)+sigma0^2/(1-q/n)-V^*(sigma)}.
Prove that a nearest-to-balanced count is minimax. With p_n=floor(n/2)/n<=1/2, prove by a complete case split over the clipped-oracle regions sigma1/sigma0<1/3, in [1/3,3], and >3 that the supremum over the full box is attained at sigma1=u,sigma0=ell; write this orientation with indexed coordinates (or as (ell,u) if tuple order is (sigma0,sigma1)), not ambiguously as (u,ell). Thus
Psi^=_{n,1}=u^2/p_n+ell^2/(1-p_n)-V^*(sigma1=u,sigma0=ell).
For odd n, retain this exact formula (equivalently 2nu^2/(n-1)+2nell^2/(n+1)-V^*) and note that the ceiling count has the symmetric opposite worst orientation and the same minimax value. For even n, both variance orientations tie at p_n=1/2; evaluate V^* explicitly to obtain (u-ell)^2 for u<=3ell and 2u^2/3-2ell^2 for u>=3ell, continuous at u=3ell. Explicitly correct the reviewer premise: the latter value does not arise only from the opposite orientation and is not zero for (sigma1,sigma0)=(u,ell). Do not strengthen assumptions, add a crux assumption, weaken the exact-B frontier, or invent a constant."
why: The reviewer identified a genuine presentation/proof gap but its numerical claim about zero regret uses ambiguous tuple ordering. Novelty remains clear and the core exact-B topic is unaffected, so one bounded repair is preferable to switching angles.
